minutes.headline: Town Meeting passed the FY16 budget, capital plan and stabilization deposit; preservation district bylaw still in debate
minutes.summary: The 2015 annual Town Meeting honored a retiring planning board member, heard the cable access report, and passed the consent articles, budget adjustments, union contract transfers, capital plan, the general budget, stabilization deposit, enterprise funds and school easements. The long Article 26 architectural preservation district debate was still open when the captions end.

public_comment.topic: Asked about the library management system in the capital plan and borrowing terms.
Asked why the town hall is not painted and why old article balances stayed unspent.
Asked for per-student cost in Lunenburg, Monty Tech and school choice.
Asked about the expenditure increase and why snow removal is budgeted below actual spending.
Asked about unfunded retirement and health care liabilities.
Asked about free cash, the stabilization balance and publicizing bond ratings.
Asked about sewer capacity bought from Fitchburg and the development behind Walmart.
Supported Article 26 and proposed lengthening review deadlines from 20 to 45 days.
Objected to unrestricted paint colors in the preservation district.
Opposed Article 26 as more bureaucracy; moved to remove 82 Highland Street from the map.
Objected that map properties may not have been properly noticed.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the general FY16 operating budget; the minutes record the vote as passed, without a count.
The two-thirds vote on the capital plan passed, funded from reappropriated balances, cash and borrowing for a dump truck and a street sweeper.
A stabilization fund deposit passed unanimously; the minutes say it maintains a five percent reserve.
Sewer, solid waste and water enterprise budgets passed, with no rate increase for sewer and no price change for solid waste bags.
The Article 26 architectural preservation district bylaw was still in debate when the captions end, and the minutes record no vote.

why_it_matters: The operating budget, the capital plan and the start of the middle-high school debt exclusion in FY16 together shape the next tax bill, and sewer and trash rates are unchanged.
If Article 26 is adopted, property owners inside the mapped district would face design review and review deadlines, so the outcome and the map's notice are things to check.
watch_next: The outcome of Article 26, which the captions do not show, including any amendment on review deadlines the moderator asked to be written down.
Any answer from the capital planning chair on town hall next year.
